HKMA announces "ART" Framework to promote responsible AI adoption Source: HKSAR Government Press Releases. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced today (October 15) the "ART" Framework to support the responsible adoption of AI in the banking sector, fostering an AI-enabled banking ecosystem with "Accountability", "Resilience", and "Trust". The Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Photo source: reference image. AI systems are becoming more autonomous, with greater access to data, tools and workflows. With the aim of supporting banks in seizing the opportunities presented by AI while maintaining robust governance and operational resilience, key initiatives under the "ART" Framework include:. Issued the latest Supervisory Guidance for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence, drawing on insights from the second cohort of the Generative AI(GenAI) Sandbox ;. An AItraining data sharing platform in collaboration with Hong Kong Cyberport Management Company Limited (Cyberport) and the University of Hong Kong, with data quality assurance as a core design principle; and. Further testing of agentic AIapplications through the GenA. I. Sandbox++ and an upcoming discussion paper on a proposed supervisory framework for agentic A. I. governance, exploring intent-anchored accountability, a registry of material AIagents, and effective intervention mechanisms. The HKMA is also co-hosting the two-day Finance+A. I. Forum with Cyberport on October 15 and 16, marking the successful completion of the technical trials under the second cohort of the GenAI Sandbox, which delivered positive results. Notably, more than 60 per cent of the use cases explored agentic AI, demonstrating the industry's active pursuit of advanced AI applications, such as automated planning and execution of multi-step tasks within defined boundaries and controls. Deputy Chief Executive of the HKMA Mr Arthur Yuen said, "The progression from generative to agentic AI represents an important new stage of innovation for the banking sector. Under Fintech 2030 , the HKMA is introducing the 'ART' Framework, which stands for 'Accountability', 'Resiliency' and 'Trust', with the aim of providing a clear foundation for banks to develop and deploy AI responsibly. By pairing innovation with clear accountability, resilient operating models and effective human oversight, banks can fully realise the benefits of AI while maintaining the trust and stability for Hong Kong's financial system. title: Sampath Bank wins regional award for AI banking
excerpt: . From left; Kiruparan Balachandran, Chief Manager - Principal Data Scientist, Sampath Bank PLC; Darshin Pathinayake, Chief Business Intelligence Officer, Sampath Bank PLC and K. G. Sampath Bank PLC has been recognised for its use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), receiving a Special Appreciation Award for AI/ML Implementation in Banking at the ICC Emerging Asia Banking Conclave & Awards 2026 in New Delhi, India. The bank was the only Sri Lankan financial institution to receive the recognition at the regional awards organised by the Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC). The awards recognise financial institutions across the BIMSTEC region for excellence and innovation, with the AI/ML category focusing on the effective use of emerging technologies to improve performance, operational efficiency and long-term value. The awards were assessed by an independent panel of former banking and regulatory leaders, with PwC India serving as process reviewer. Sampath Bank Chief Business Intelligence Officer Darshin Pathinayake said the award reflected the bank’s commitment to using data, analytics, AI and ML to improve customer engagement, operational efficiency, risk management and decision-making. Pathinayake and Principal Data Scientist Kiruparan Balachandran represented the bank at the event. Pathinayake also participated in a panel discussion on trust, technology and transformation, which covered digital transformation, cyber resilience, regulatory developments and collaboration among banks, fintech companies and technology partners. title: APAC banks favour AI fraud detection amidst security fears
excerpt: 2 hours ago. Infographic generated using artificial intelligence (AI). APAC banks favour AI fraud detection amidst security fears. FICO found that 42% of executives cited data privacy and protection as their biggest adoption barrier. More than 60% of banking leaders in Asia-Pacific (APAC) identified fraud and scam detection as the area where generative artificial intelligence (AI) could most improve operations in the next 12 months, according to a survey by analytics software company FICO. Underwriting decisions were cited by 21% of respondents, followed by customer-facing digital banking services at 15% and regulatory compliance monitoring at 3%. Join Asian Banking & Finance community. The findings come as banks seek to adopt AI tools designed specifically for financial services. Some 77% of respondents said it was extremely important for banking AI tools to be purpose-built, whilst the remaining 23% considered this somewhat important. Data privacy and security were the biggest barriers to adoption, cited by 42% of respondents. Regulatory and compliance risks and model transparency and explainability were each identified by 21%. Only 16% cited computing costs or infrastructure as their main concern. Dattu Kompella, FICO’s managing director for APAC, said banks need AI models that can explain their decisions, be audited and meet regulatory requirements. Banks also expect purpose-built AI to become more widely used in the coming years. Nearly half of respondents, or 46%, expect task-specific AI models to be deployed in fraud , compliance and underwriting within one to two years. Another 26% expect adoption within three to five years, whilst 26% said their organisations had already deployed such models. Beyond fraud prevention, 64% identified credit underwriting and lending decisions as the back-office processes that would benefit most from purpose-built AI. Regulatory compliance monitoring was cited by 18%, customer due diligence by 10% and internal policy and business operations reviews by 8%. The survey was conducted in August 2026 during FICO’s Banking Leaders Forum in Bali, gathering responses from 51 senior executives and C-suite leaders at banks across APAC.
